  line clear whenever its far end is far - exactly the "from inside him to beyond him" line the predicate exists to refuse;
- **the shoulder nodes did not exist.** The earlier pass's review (`docs/reviews/2026-11-14-d211-clearance.md`) and the code's own doc comment both described them; `grep shoulder`
  found the comment and nothing else. The two `clearance.rs` fixtures passed without them, because the stander's *tile* was
  in the avoid set and a whole-tile rectangle existed to bend round - so the sub-tile claim was never exercised. It is now,
  by two tests that call `short_range_clear` directly with a hand-built `Walk` and no world under them.

**What it costs, and what was never isolated.** D211 landed in the same step as the correction to D210's tie-break (a loser
that paused itself stood for ever), so the acceptance run it first produced - 42,378 / 43,049 ms against `main`'s
30,970 / 30,757 ms, `repaths_body 83 -> 446` - is **both changes at once** and cannot be charged to this decision alone.
That was reported as such rather than dressed up. What can be said now, with D213 in (the stander set finally fed), is
that the search's own cost is not what dominates: the same match runs at `main`'s wall-clock (42,283 / 42,322 ms against
42,596 / 41,896 ms) with `repaths` **380 against 765** and `repaths_body` **121 against 446**, because a plan routes round a
standing man instead of colliding with him and re-planning. The added work per plan - eight nodes per body, a disc test per
edge, `O(n^2)` in nodes - is real and still unmeasured per plan: `crates/sim/tests/perf.rs` at a fixed entity count is the
measurement owed for it.

**Basis.** The DE talk's method (*shrink the units to points, expand the obstacles, be careful with the start and the end*,
`docs/archive/research/pathfinding-from-the-talk.md`); `FUN_007f9d80` for the per-search body list; measurement in
`docs/reviews/2026-11-14-d211-clearance.md` and its follow-up.


### D212 - a search that starts inside a body is re-seeded at twice the clearance, and only *away* from him

*Date:* 2026-11-14

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

**What it says.** `FUN_007fb220`, the low-level search: it asks whether its **start** point is inside an obstruction, and if
so it offsets the start by **`2 x radius`** along each direction of a fixed table, re-seeds the search at the first free
one, and returns `3` ("no low-level path") only when every direction is blocked.

**What it builds.** The same re-seed in `short_range_clear`: when the start is inside a body's clearance, a fixed ring of
eight directions is tried at `2 x clearance`, and the first candidate that is free of every disc becomes the head of the
route.

**What the binary alone does not settle, and measurement did.** A candidate on the **far side** of the man is free, and
walking to it means walking through him: measured 3702 raw against an 8000 reach, worse than doing nothing (4207). A free
point beyond a man you are already inside is a *destination*, not a place to start. So the anchor must move **away** from
every disc the start is inside - the same rule the graph's first edges use (`step_out_ok`), because it is the same question.

**Basis.** `FUN_007fb220` and the direction table at `0x9e252c` (read 2026-11-14); the talk's "be careful about the start and
end points"; measurement in `docs/reviews/2026-11-14-d211-clearance.md`.


### D213 - `last_moved` is the tick a body last *moved*, or the tick it came into being

*Date:* 2026-11-14

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

**What it says.** The original keeps a per-unit `+0x134 lastMoveTime` and compares it with the tick a search returned
(`path+0x10`) to decide whether a collider is **past** - "he has not moved since I planned round this, so my route already
accounts for him" (D210). Two of our rules read that one field: the *past* test, and the stander sets that make a body at
rest an obstacle to the search that meets it (D210b). The original's own search inserts an object when its **velocity is
zero** (`FUN_007f9d80`), which is the same fact seen from the other side.

**The defect, measured.** `move_bodies` wrote `last_moved = now` at **both** of its write sites unconditionally, so every
body in the tick's delta list was stamped - including an `Idle` one and one standing its pause out. A stopped villager's
`last_moved` advanced on every tick it stood still. Both readers were therefore dead: `created >= moved` can only hold for
a route planned the same tick, so nothing was ever past; and the stander sets answered "nobody", so the only body a plan
treated as ground was the one a re-plan named explicitly. Measured on
`clearance::a_man_who_stopped_before_the_route_was_planned_is_routed_round`: **7686 raw** against an 8000 reach, the plan a
straight line through the man.

**What it builds.** One choke point - the `movers` loop, which already holds the bodies whose decided step was non-zero -
stamps the field, and nothing else does. Every construction site (`seed`, `Command::Spawn`, training, a foundation, a
projectile) initialises it to `self.tick`, because the *second* half of the bug is that a body which has never moved keeps
`0`, and `created >= 0` is true of every route: a body spawned **after** a walker planned looked past, and the walker walked
through a man who did not exist when he planned. Three fixtures caught that within a minute of the first fix
(`evasion`, `step_decision`, `repath_reasons`, each reporting "the scene never met the body").

**What it changes.** The two rules become live, so a route now plans *round* a man who is standing rather than through him,
and a collider older than the route is dropped. Three fixtures were restated because the rule now works: the encounter they
measured was avoided rather than forced, so the stander is placed after the route exists
(`collision::a_walker_never_ends_a_tick_inside_a_friend`), and two others simply stopped seeing a "past" body.

**What it costs.** Nothing measurable, and the searches it was feared to multiply are *gone*: interleaved A/B on the
acceptance match (`--seed 7 --ticks 48000`, release), `main` 42,596 / 41,896 ms against 42,283 / 42,322 ms - **the same
wall-clock** - while `repaths` fall **765 -> 380** and `repaths_body` **446 -> 121 (-73%)**, because a plan now routes round
a standing man instead of walking into him and re-planning afterwards. The match is still won (the enemy town centre razed at
1,919.2 s against 1,857.2 s, with 144 entities against 133). D210b's 2.3x was measured with this field broken: the stander set
was fed nothing, so the search failed more often and every failure ran the whole-route fallback.

**Basis.** `+0x134` and `path+0x10` (`docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`, read 2026-11-14); `FUN_007f9d80` for the per-search
body list; the field's own doc comment, which the code contradicted. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-15-d213-last-moved.md`.


### D236 - villagers walk through each other, and both obvious fixes starve the match (2026-11-16, nothing landed but the specification)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

**The owner's report, and what is *not* the cause.** *"Villagers push each other. That may never happen. Villager has to reroute,
never push the other villager away"* - seen in window mode. Displacement was already gone: `push_the_standing` was deleted by
D207/D208/D210 and `made_room` is a dead counter that always reads 0. Two other mechanisms produce the same look, and one of
them is the one he saw:

1. **A group walks over itself (D207).** Every unit ordered to move in the same tick became a path-ignore "mate" of the others
   and the collider was dropped outright. The window submits one walk per selected unit in one tick, so a box-select and a
   right-click turn the selection into a crowd that passes through itself. The original has this exemption, but the list it
   filters is the *formation's* members, and Forgotten Empires' own documentation puts villagers, trade carts and fishing ships
   in no formation - *"each of them takes their own path"* (`docs/prior-art.md`, `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`).
2. **A node's ring is re-laid** when it refuses a man (D200), and the re-lay re-assigns every man on the node.

**Both fixes were built and both were measured, and both were worse than the defect.**
- **Narrow the exemption to soldiers** (villagers solid): the acceptance match **starved**. Seed 7, 48,000 ticks, release:
  entities **149 → 139**, `repaths` **432 → 1,401** - and the split moves the *other* way, body **90 → 22** and ground
  **342 → 1,379**: the men are no longer blocked by bodies, they are re-planning round the ground for ever - and five `gather`
  fixtures went red. A villager crowd
  that may not pass over itself has nothing to route round a body with: `STALLED_TICKS` is 40, i.e. two seconds of standing per
  encounter, and forty men round a woodline spend the match standing.
- **Keep the exemption and put a body back when it lands deeper than it started** (the original's pause-the-higher-id answer,
  applied as a post-step separation pass): the same starvation and the same **1,401** repaths, because the gather ring's own
  approaches are deeper than the standoff by construction - the ring seats men 0.66 apart and they pass within 0.2 of each other
  on the way in.

Both were reverted. The tree is back to `2f1ab0ae663e2506` at 48,000 ticks (149 entities, 432 repaths), which is the baseline.

**What is left in the tree.** `crates/sim/tests/overlap.rs`: the **specification**, with the rule as the game states it - an
encounter may reach contact and may never get deeper (`collision::a_walker_never_ends_a_tick_inside_a_friend` pins the pair's
version of the same thing). `eight_villagers_ordered_to_one_tile_never_walk_through_each_other` is **red on today's engine** and
is `#[ignore]`d with the reason; on the pre-fix tree it reports *"villagers (9700, 9702) got 0.346 tiles apart at tick 101,
deeper than the 0.372 they first touched at"*, which is the defect in one line. The second fixture,
`a_newcomer_does_not_move_the_working_gatherers`, is **green and mutation-proved**: a re-lay that wipes the seats reddens it
(`villager 9800 lost the place it was working`), so the seats survive a re-lay today and that is now pinned.

**Why nothing landed, in one sentence.** The owner's rule is right and the engine cannot yet obey it cheaply: making villagers
solid needs a **body-aware replan** - a route that goes *round* a body, which is D210b's remaining half - and without it the
crowd deadlocks into the same failure D205 measured. The fix is a slice of its own, not a flag.

**Basis.** `crates/sim/src/world/step.rs` (`stamp_group`, `maybe_respawn`→`maybe_respread`, `move_bodies`), `crates/sim/src/
world/movement.rs` (`blocker_at`, the mate and "past" clauses), `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md` (the path-ignore list),
`docs/prior-art.md` (openaok, genie, openage, the formations page), and the two acceptance runs above. Review:
`docs/reviews/2026-11-16-d236-overlap-and-reroute.md`.


### D237 - villagers are solid, and the fix was a guard nobody had looked at (2026-11-16)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

**What D236 got wrong, first.** D236 concluded the narrowing was blocked on "a route that goes round a body (D210b's remaining
half)". The route already exists: on a body collision the mover asks for a `Repath { body }`, and the replan builds discs for the
men in the way and calls `short_range_clear` over them - the **pencil** (D211) that bends a route round a disc. What refused the
request was one condition: `if !near_goal && ...`, written for *ground* (a search beside the goal buys nothing, D98a) and fatal
for *bodies*, because a gatherer's whole life is spent within one tile of his goal. A blocked villager could not ask for a route
at all; he stood for `STALLED_TICKS` (two seconds) and, with the mates exemption still in place, his crowd never noticed. Narrow
the exemption and every blocked man stands in the last tile for ever - which is the starvation D236 measured (149 entities to
139, `repaths` 432 to 1,401) and blamed on a missing mechanism.

**What landed, two changes.**
1. **`stamp_group` forms mates among soldiers only** (D207's scope narrowed): the original's path-ignore list filters a
   *formation's* members, and Forgotten Empires' own documentation puts villagers, trade carts and fishing ships in no formation
   (*"each of them takes their own path"*). A villager ordered with others is now solid to them.
2. **A body in the way may be planned round inside the goal's own tile** (`(!near_goal || a_unit)`): the near-goal guard keeps
   its ground half and loses its body half, bounded exactly as before - one search per man per wait (`stalled.remove`), and
   `MAX_REPATHS_PER_TICK`.

**Measured, acceptance match, seed 7, 48,000 ticks, release, both binaries built from source and interleaved:**

| | entities | `repaths` (body / ground) | hash | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | 149 | 432 (90 / 342) | `2f1ab0ae663e2506` | 36.82 s, 37.97 s |
| this | **155** | 497 (139 / 358) | `8cf433ad4e0205f4` | 38.36 s, 38.45 s |

**+2.7%** on the same scenario (median 37.39 s against 38.41 s, two interleaved pairs) and **+15%** on body repaths - and six
more entities alive at 48,000 ticks than before, i.e. the crowd routes instead of deadlocking. The hash moves because the
behaviour changed, which is the point of the slice and not a defect.

**What it fixes.** A box-selected crowd of villagers no longer walks over itself: `crates/sim/tests/overlap.rs`'s
`eight_villagers_ordered_to_one_tile_never_walk_through_each_other` was red on the old engine (0.346 tiles apart at tick 101,
deeper than its 0.372 first contact) and is green now, back off `#[ignore]`. The rule it asserts is the game's, not a stricter
invention: an encounter may reach contact and may never get deeper.

**Fixtures restated, because two of them were about to become vacuous.** `crates/sim/tests/group_overlap.rs` pinned the group
rule with **villagers** in two fixtures; with villagers never being mates they would still have passed, by never forming a
group at all. Both now spawn **spearmen** - the units the rule is actually about - through a shared `spawn_unit` helper.

**Basis.** `crates/sim/src/world/step.rs` (`stamp_group`), `crates/sim/src/world/movement.rs` (the near-goal clause), the pencil
in `world/pathing` (`short_range_clear`, discs), `crates/sim/tests/overlap.rs`, `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md` (the path-ignore
list), `docs/prior-art.md` (the formations page). Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-16-d237-villagers-solid.md`.


### D239 - The game is the source of truth on pathing: every divergence adopted, and two rules of ours deleted (owner, 2026-11-16)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

The owner, over the movement rows of the register (`docs/archive/research/behaviour-diff.md`): *"Resolve the questions by adopting from the game.
That is the source of truth."* Every divergent row therefore becomes a slice, and **where the game's side is unread the read comes
first** - the tree does not get a guess in the game's name.

**Adopted as read - the binary, the talk or his own saves answer:**

1. **A body at rest is not walked through** (row 29). `collide` rule 6 (`TakeAtRest`) takes a step through an idle body after
   asking for a repath, so the route round him is installed *after* he has been stepped through. The original's epilogue has four
   arms - target / non-past re-path / pause / *"Don't know what to do about my collision(s)"* - and this is not one: an idle
   friend who is not past is a non-past collision. Rule 6 goes.
2. **A re-plan does not plan round what it met, and does not accumulate** (row 30). We fold `route.avoiding` into the search as
   **obstacle tiles** (`step.rs:1325`) and keep every body ever met for the life of the route; the game writes its ignore list
   *after* the search and reads it **only in the classifier**. The search loses the set; the classifier keeps it.
3. **The pause is re-drawn on a fresh collision** (row 18, corrected from `same`). `setPause` (`0x8aa6d0`) writes the path's timer
   with no "already paused" guard; ours stands the first draw.
4. **A paused mate stops being a mate** (row 20, corrected). The exemption is re-tested every tick on `isMoving`
   (`[vtbl+0x2a0]`); ours ends it when the route is dropped, and a paused man keeps his route.
5. **A man with no seat** (rows 24, 25), **as the owner ruled it on 2026-11-16 and corrected the same day**: the node's ring
   is not re-laid (D238 measured that shuffle at 0.52 tiles, `SEATMOVE`), and a man who cannot get a square looks for **another
   bush nearby** - within `gather_reach`, the worker's line of sight plus five tiles (D149) - and **waits** when there is none.
   That is D204 as built, and the owner's own words are its statement: *"if there is no other bush nearby, then worker waits for
   free spot, if there is another bush nearby, he will go work there."* **What retires is only the idle-body nudge.** *This
   paragraph first said the newcomer "keeps circling this node", which was my reading of his earlier sentence and was wrong*; the
   correction is his, made in the same conversation, and the row now says `same` for the re-target and `different` for the nudge.
   **D238's "a seated body must not be past" stands withdrawn**: under the game's own past test a stopped man *is* past and is
   walked through, and the original keeps bodies apart with the **seats**, not with the collision.
6. **An unreachable waypoint is substituted, not waited on** (row 26): `mConsecutiveSubstituteCount` - *"we have a count of %d,
   faking it"*. `finish_blocked_orders` (the order dies where the man stands after forty refused ticks) retires in its favour.
7. **Passage is the body's** (row 21): **supersedes D117**. The ground a body may cross is the ground grown by its radius; the tile
   graph grows too, and a 0.5-radius unit has no passage in a one-tile gap. The step layer already did this (D176/D192), so the
   change is one layer and the test that inverts is `a_big_unit_walks_through_a_one_tile_gap`.

**Adopted, with a read in front of it - neither may be ported on a guess:**

8. **The cost model and the frontier** (row 13): 16 per cardinal step and a load-time octile table rather than 10/14 with a
   product; and the per-tile best-cost array with a generation stamp rather than a heap, because equal-cost ordering is what a
   route's shape depends on. **Blocked on the number that does not fit**: the estimate reads 2500/100 per unit against a
   16-per-step cost, which is not admissible in tile units, so either those arguments are not tiles or 16 is not the step cost.
9. **Two levels with a parent** (row 27): a high-level path built when the low-level one fails, and *"we don't have a parent path,
   so we're stopping"*. Blocked on reading `AddFuturePath`'s derivation.

**Added the same day by the sibling thread, and adopted on the same rule:** **33** the start is re-seeded when the mover
stands inside a body (`FUN_007fb220`) - missing, with the pencil's outward-only edge as its stand-in; and **36** the order's
path vocabulary (forced waypoint, teleport-to-waypoint, per-path hit) is narrower here. Rows 31, 34 and 35 read as `same`
(D134's closest-standing-point, the pause enforced twice, the straight line before the search) and take no slice; row 32 - a
*thing* whose route fails - stays `unknown-static` because the talk settles the search and not the task layer.

**Nothing is ruled out of adoption.** Row 22's two caps (`MAX_GROUND_REPLANS = 2`, `MAX_REPATHS_PER_TICK = 4`) go with the rest,
and the **3.5-against-0.3 ms/tick** price that justified them was taken before the sub-tile pencil existed, so the slice
**re-measures** and puts the number in its review. A regression found there is a finding for the owner; it is not a licence to
reinstate a rule the game does not have.

**What adoption cannot settle:** row 23, the exclusive goal - no read decides it and no decision should stand in for the recording
of **forty units ordered to one tile**, which is the cheapest artefact in the register.

**Order and gates**: `docs/next-step.md`. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-16-d239-adopt-the-game.md`.


### D241 - Four pathing rulings the game cannot settle, and one of them was already built (owner, 2026-11-16)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

The owner, answering the forks that the original's behaviour leaves open:

1. **A stopped man is walked through** - *"follow game"*. So D210's **past** rule stands for every body, D238's step 1 stays
   withdrawn, and an idle friend is not a wall to a route planned after he stopped. The consequence is deliberate and named:
   two bodies can be seen overlapping where one is routed through a man who has stopped, and what the game does about it is the
   **pause**, not a shove.
2. **Formations are deferred; villagers are solid.** *"unit formation is to be implemented later"* - so the mate exemption keeps
   its same-tick stand-in for **soldiers**, and is documented as a stand-in rather than as the rule; a formation kind is a later
   slice behind `stamp_group`. For **villagers** the game's rule is already ours: villagers join no formation, so they are solid
   to each other (D237).
3. **A thing that cannot be reached.** Two cases, in the owner's words: a tree behind a **wall** - the man tries to find a path,
   and failing that *"will approach the tree as much as he can and idle"*; a tree behind **other trees** - he approaches as close
   to the tree he was sent to as he can *"and start working on the nearest tree"*. Today the order is **refused at order time**
   (`orders.rs:52`), so this is a slice: accept it, plan to the nearest reachable point, and when the target is a resource node
   prefer a reachable node of the same kind within `gather_reach` - the same helper the no-seat rule already uses, at a different
   trigger.
4. **A crowd at a bush** - *"if there is no other bush nearby, then worker waits for free spot, if there is another bush nearby,
   he will go work there."* **Already built**: after forty refused ticks `count_refused_squares` asks `nearest_like_free` and
   re-targets, or stands the man down to wait (`step.rs:2178-2212`). What remains is the **incumbent** half only - no re-lay
   (`maybe_respread`) and no nudge.

**What this corrects, and it is my error:** D239 and the D204 withdrawal marker said the next-node re-target was retired. It is
not - the re-target **is** the owner's rule and **is** what the code does; only the displacement goes. Register rows 24 and 32
are amended to say so, and row 24 now reads `same` for the re-target and `different` for the nudge.

**A consequence worth stating before it is measured:** with the past rule standing (ruling 1), the **0.204-tile pile** D238 caught
is no longer a defect - it is what the game does when a route is planned through a man who has stopped. The fixture that pins this
must therefore assert what the owner actually objects to (**nobody is shoved off his square**), not that no two bodies ever
overlap; the old assertion would now be the old rule speaking.

**Basis.** `docs/archive/research/behaviour-diff.md` rows 24, 25, 32; `crates/sim/src/world/step.rs` (the refusal count, the retarget, the nudge),
`crates/sim/src/world/gather.rs` (`nearest_like_free`, `gather_reach`), `crates/sim/src/world/orders.rs:52`. Review:
`docs/reviews/2026-11-16-d241-rulings.md`.


### D242 - R1 measured: both halves of the game's answer cost the match more than they buy (2026-11-16, nothing landed)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

D239 adopted the game's pathing answers wholesale; `docs/next-step.md` turned every divergent row into a slice (R1-R9). R1 was
the first: **row 29** (a body at rest that is not past is walked through) and **row 30** (the re-plan folds the bodies it has
already met into the search's obstacle tiles). Both halves were built and measured separately, and **both were reverted**.

**Half 1 - the step through a body at rest (`TakeAtRest`).** Deleting the arm works: a walker sent past a stopped friend, who
moved *after* the route was planned (so he is genuinely not past), comes no closer than the pair's reach - measured 8,000 raw in
8,000, against 7,200 before. But it **deadlocks two soldiers in a lane**: `group_overlap::two_units_ordered_apart_are_not_a_group_
and_the_loser_pauses` stands at *"both have to arrive: a at (5,1), b at (5,2) after 2002 ticks"*, and
`a_mate_who_is_stopped_becomes_solid` never meets at all. The game resolves exactly this with the **past** rule: the paused man
stops moving, the other's re-plan is stamped later, and the stopped man becomes past - and that chain does not complete in this
engine. The arm therefore stays, and `crates/sim/tests/replan.rs::a_stopped_friend_is_not_walked_through` is `#[ignore]`d as the
specification for the slice that completes it.

**Half 2 - the search stops receiving the avoid set.** Also built, also reverted: **entities 155 -> 143** and `repaths`
**380 -> 649** at 48,000 ticks. The reason is in the same reading that motivated the change: the original's search *does*
insert a standing object into its per-search rectangle list (`FUN_007f9d80`), and the bodies it does not re-insert are the ones
the classifier has answered for. In this engine the pencil (`stander_bodies`) supplies the first and `route.avoiding` supplied
the second; remove the second and every re-plan meets the same men again - a 71% increase in re-paths and twelve fewer entities
alive at the end.

**What that says about the queue.** R1's two rows are not two small deletions; each is a deletion *plus* the mechanism that
makes the game's rule pay for itself (the past-rule chain; a search that re-reads standers instead of remembering them). The
queue's gate - **entities at or above 155, `repaths` near 380** - is what caught it, exactly as `docs/next-step.md` intended.
R2-R9 are unchanged and unblocked; R1 is split in the queue into **R1a** (the past-rule chain, which unblocks the arm) and
**R1b** (the avoid set, which needs the stander re-read first).

**Basis.** `crates/sim/src/world/movement.rs` (rule 6, the arm), `crates/sim/src/world/step.rs` (the re-plan's `obstacles`),
`crates/sim/tests/replan.rs` (the ignored fixture), `crates/sim/tests/group_overlap.rs` (the deadlock, measured),
`docs/archive/research/behaviour-diff.md` rows 29-30. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-16-d242-r1-measured.md`.


### D247 - the original's pathing rules are a separate conformance set, not part of the gate (2026-11-16)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

**What it says.** `crates/conformance` asserts the pathfinding and obstacle-avoidance rules of the original against this
engine's planners, as its own set with its own command (`make conformance`), and **not** in the pre-commit gate:

- **One rule per test**, the source named in the test's doc comment - `samuelcaldas/age-of-empires-2-decomp`'s `src/zone/`
  modules for the shape, HD's own sites (`FUN_007ffd10`, `FUN_007f9d80`, `FUN_007fb220`) for the numbers.
- **A rule the game keeps and we do not is `#[ignore]`d with its reason and its decision**, never asserted green and never
  left red in the gate - so `-- --ignored` prints the register of where we stand apart, and a later slice shows it closed.
- **A defect it finds about our own code is `findings.rs`**, same treatment: red on purpose, filed with the number that
  proves it, fixed in its own slice.

**Why.** Asked on 2026-11-16 whether the original's pathing rules could be pinned as tests "for the project as extra set ran
separately". The value is the register: D239 adopted the game's pathing wholesale and rows 13-33 of
`docs/archive/research/behaviour-diff.md` each owe a slice, so a set that states the game's rule and our answer in one place makes the queue
checkable rather than remembered. It is out of the gate because a conformance test's job is to *disagree* when we diverge;
putting disagreement into the gate either turns every commit red or teaches everyone to weaken the test.

**Provenance and its limits.** The repo carries **no licence** (all rights reserved), so it is read for behaviour and cited
by module - no expression is transcribed. Its addresses are AoC/PS2, not HD 5.7, so every number is pinned to HD's own site
instead; and its C bodies are reconstructions of PS2 assembly (at least one loops `w` for both axes), so a claim enters the
table only where the masks, the node layout or a first-party source agrees.

**What it found on landing.** `nearest_reachable` answers **one step from the start**, not the tile nearest the click: on
empty ground from (1,1) toward (10,10) the answer is (2,2), because every tile its frontier pushes is already free, so the
first pop is a neighbour of the start. Its own doc comment and D134's "nearest legal standing point" claim the opposite, and
`click_into_the_woods.rs` misses it by spawning the villager one tile from the wood. Filed as `findings.rs`; the fix owes its
own slice and its own measurement.

**Commits us to.** Keeping the set's findings and divergences visible rather than green; and adding a rule to
`docs/archive/research/pathfinding-conformance.md`'s table when one is read, with the module that settles it.


### D248 - the four body rules hold, and the seat is the reason they did not (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

The owner's four invariants are **green and unskipped** (`crates/sim/tests/invariants.rs`: 4 passed, 0 ignored), by five changes
that belong together:

1. **Places are dealt at least one diameter apart** (`maybe_respread`). The ring is generated per tile, so candidates from
   neighbouring tiles sat **0.2** apart and were handed out anyway; the per-tick band correction existed to push men out of each
   other afterwards. With the separation enforced at the deal, the places are right when they are given.
2. **A working man's place is frozen** (`maybe_respread`). The re-lay re-seated *every* worker nearest-first, so a newcomer could
   move a man already taking from the node - D238's `SEATMOVE`, and the owner's *"villager is never to be nudged to leave place he
   is working at"*.
3. **A man on his own place is not stepped** (the settle, `on_own_place` within a twentieth of a tile). This is rule 4; the
   fixture caught a **0.011-tile** step at tick 11 while he was taking wood.
4. **A man already taking does not walk at the node either.** `settling` was false because he stood on his place, so the tick fell
   through to the walk branch and moved him **0.011** toward the node.
5. **A load banks at the wall.** The delivery test is `footprint_gap(position, drop) <= radius + one step`, and the fallback aim
   is `World::wall_point` - the footprint grown by the radius - because a tile centre beside a footprint is **half a tile** from
   it, so a carrier aiming at one can never come within his own radius.

**The defect the first four exposed, which is the real find.** With the settle no longer nudging a man already on his place,
nothing re-examined a worker's route: a woodcutter stood at `(24.5, 12.2)` for **400,000 ticks**, `progress 0`, **clearance 528**,
his own place **0.03 tiles** away, and a waypoint **0.73 tiles** away that the collision rule refused every tick - the bank stuck
at **890 of 900** (`research::two_players_can_be_different_civilizations`, 128 s against 38 s at HEAD). The cause is the aim, not
the budget: the route ended on the **node's own blocked tile**, so he pressed at a wall for ever. **A gatherer never aims at the
node's tile**: when the next waypoint is on it, the aim is his own place, which is walkable ground beside the node. The test is
back to **22 s**. A time-armed re-plan budget (`REPLAN_EVERY`, because `Route::stalls` is per *route* and can never re-arm) was
built first and **removed**: 5,214 re-paths in that fixture and the bank still stuck at 890, and it took the acceptance match from
~500 to **10,323** re-paths. Measuring it is why it is not in the tree.

**Mutation proof, both directions**: the old tile-adjacency delivery test reddens rule 3 at **0.321 tiles**; removing the
on-own-place gate reddens rule 4 at **0.011 tiles**.

**Not claimed**: the acceptance re-path count is higher than D237's 497 and no interleaved wall-time pair was taken, so no
percentage is claimed here. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-17-d248-seats-and-walls.md` (and the patch it carried, now applied).


### D250 - the owner's second four rules, and the four defects they found (2026-11-16)

*Date:* 2026-11-16

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner, 2026-11-16: **"Please add unit tests never to be skipped or ignored: If villager or any other unit circle crosses
tile (approaches closer than 1/2 diameter) with resource that has not been depleted yet (mine, bush, tree...) -> FAIL. If
villager or any other unit circle crosses tile ... with building under the construction (except farm) or finished building
(except farm and walkable part of town center) -> FAIL. If villager constructs farm while not inside it (at least 1/2
diameter inside farm plot) -> FAIL. If technology that is not available at current age (for example Imperial Age in Dark Age)
shows -> FAIL."***

Four fixtures, none `#[ignore]`d, in the file the first four live in plus the card's own file: rule 5 and 6 in
`crates/sim/tests/invariants.rs` over the same 2,000-tick economy (**every tick**, every unit, every live node and every
footprint), rule 7 over a farm being raised, rule 8 in `crates/sim/tests/card_age.rs` where the towers of cards are actually
built. Two of the four held on the engine as it stood (**5** the resource tile, and **6**'s finished-building half) - and four
of the rules turned out to be broken once the test asked about the **body** instead of the tile.

1. **A builder started a house from 0.02 tiles outside its footprint** (rule 6). `Task::Build` asked whether his **tile**
   touched the footprint, so a man still walking past was "adjacent" the moment his centre crossed into a neighbouring
   tile; the first stroke then made those tiles solid with his own circle **0.18 tiles inside** them - the crossing the rule
   forbids, caused by the builder himself. Fixed: the work test is the body's clearance from the footprint (`apart >= radius`,
   Euclidean, integer), not tile adjacency.
2. **The site-clear gate counted unit tiles, so a body at the edge was walled in** (rule 6, D183 §5's promise). A body
   spawned 0.1 tiles from the footprint's edge has its tile outside the site, so the gate said "clear" and the first stroke
   landed on it: **tick 25, 0.1 tiles inside the wall**. Fixed: `site_is_clear` counts a unit whose **circle** overlaps the
   footprint, and tells its own side to step aside; the stroke waits for the body, not for the tile.
3. **A farm was built from outside its plot** (rule 7). D183 §3's "a builder works from outside the site" is about a site
   whose first stroke raises a wall; a farm is a floor with no site-clear gate at all (D183 §7), so nothing was being held up
   and the standoff was pure loss - measured **-0.02 tiles**: the farmer 0.02 outside the plot's edge with construction
   already progressing. Fixed: a farm's build order aims at the plot's **centre** (`World::footprint_centre`) and the site
   counts as work when his **whole circle** is inside it (`inset >= radius`), which is the owner's "at least 1/2 diameter
   inside farm plot".
4. **Imperial Age showed on a Dark Age town centre's card** (rule 8). `check_research` asked the age's **building**
   requirement before its **prerequisites**, so a Dark Age player asking for the Imperial Age was told *"you need two
   castle/siege-workshop buildings"* - true, unactionable, and not what `is_age_gate` recognises as the age talking, so
   `card` drew the button. Measured on the fixture: `["villager", "loom", "feudal_age", "castle_age", "imperial_age"]`.
   Fixed: prerequisites are asked first, so the answer is *"the Castle Age is missing"* - an age gate, and the item is
   hidden. The **next** age keeps its greyed button (D243's rule that a refusal the player can act on stays), which the
   fixture asserts in the same test.

**Mutation proofs**, each the direction that matters: restoring the tile-adjacency work test reddens rule 6 at **0.02 tiles**
(builder); restoring the tile-only site-clear gate reddens it at **0.1 tiles** (bystander, tick 25); the farm standoff
reddens rule 7 at **-0.02 tiles**; the old check order reddens rule 8 on the fixture above.

**Measured on the acceptance match** (release, seed 7, 48,000 ticks, one worktree and two binaries, two interleaved runs of
each state): before **67.6 s and 68.2 s**, `entities=154 players=2 hash=95ea803822c1b341 repaths=1540` (body 236, ground
1,304); after **28.4 s and 28.5 s**, `entities=137 players=1 hash=ac2e785d9f551b55 repaths=710` (body 439, ground 271). The
difference is **the win**: the match is now decided at **2,381 s** (*"the match is over: no further orders are accepted"*, no
enemy town centre left) where the control is undecided at 48,000, so the entity drop is the loser's base being gone rather
than an economy starving - and the cost of the three body/card fixes is nil, proved by a bisect in which they leave the match
bit-identical and the farm rule alone reproduces the whole delta. **Open for the owner**: the queue's floor is entities at or
above **155** and both states read below it (154 with no win, 137 with one), so either the floor describes a contested match
and needs its own fixture, or the win is the better outcome and the floor wants restating.

**Commits us to.** No `#[ignore]` on any of these eight fixtures; a new rule arrives with its source and its sentence; a rule
the engine does not keep is **named as a finding on the engine** (D249's rule) rather than parked in an ignored test; and any
claim of the shape "a body may never be inside X" is answered about the **body**, never about the tile its centre is in -
three of the four defects above were the same mistake made in three places.


### D251 - the game's speed is the unit's own, and this engine's walk stutters at every corner (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: "villagers never slow down. They may stop or stop to repath but since they are never in the formations, there is no
reason for them to change speed. So either they walk, or stand" - and, before anything was written, "verify from the original
game and [the decomp] first. Then let me decide."*

**The game.** `getMaxVelFwd` (`008a2a30`, move_obj.cpp 3,069-3,145) returns the unit's own dat speed (`unitdef+0xe4`), multiplied
by **one** thing - a motion object's factor (`[move+0x14]+0x6c`) when that is `> 0.0` - and **exactly 0.0 on a pause**. No terrain
factor, no ramp, no partial-speed arm. The factor's only writer is the virtual setter `0x7f4130`, which has no direct caller and
is **unread**; the only mechanism that needs one is the formation (`FormationParams(..., breakAutoFormationsBySpeed=%d)`), where
villagers are never members. Read in `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`.

**The decompilation cannot help**: `samuelcaldas/age-of-empires-2-decomp` has no speed, velocity, acceleration or max-velocity
code at all - its unit movement and formation files are 16-47-line stubs, and the only "acceleration" in it is camera drag
(`docs/prior-art.md`). Recorded so nobody searches it twice.

**This engine, measured** (`crates/sim/tests/step_speed_probe.rs`, 5 villagers, 4,000 ticks): **89.00% stand, 10.93% walk a whole
step, 0.07% - 15 of 20,000 body-ticks - moved between 0.11 and 0.95 of a step**, and every one was decided `Take`: not a slide,
not a pause, not a refusal. Fourteen sat on one long `Move` where `path_length` decremented on each - a **corner's landing**: the
mover aimed at the next route point and `step_towards` lands exactly on a point within one step, so the tick spent the gap
(0.011 tiles) instead of a step. The fifteenth was an idle settle at the goal.

**The fork put to him**, with costs: (a) land the fixture `#[ignore]`d as the specification; (b) fixture and fix together; (c)
narrow the rule to the speed setting. **He chose (b)** - D252.


### D252 - a corner is folded into the step, and only a walk folds (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner chose (b), fixture and fix in one slice, and then ruled that a fixture he asked for is **never skipped**: no
`#[ignore]` without his word. The fix therefore had to land, and the diagnosis below is what it cost.*

**The rule, in his words, and corrected by him on 2026-11-17**: *"man stands or walks. No acceleration or deceleration"* - not
"one whole step". The step is the **observable form** of constant speed at a fixed tick rate, which is why the fixture measures
it, but the rule is about the speed never ramping.

**The rule, as a fixture.** `crates/sim/tests/whole_steps.rs`, two tests, neither ignored: on every tick a villager is walking, the
distance he covers **along his route** is exactly one step, or zero (a refused step, a pause, a body in the way); the only short
tick allowed is the last, which lands on the goal and may not overshoot it. Along the route and not as a straight line, because a
corner walked *through* inside a tick makes the chord shorter than the path - the chord version cannot tell a fold from a lost
tick, which is why it took three attempts.

**The defect.** The mover aims at the route's next point and `step_towards` lands exactly on a point within one step: right for the
goal, wrong for a corner, which spends the gap (**0.011 tiles, 0.107 of a step**) and loses the rest of the tick. Measured by
`step_speed_probe`: **15 of 20,000** villager body-ticks between 0.11 and 0.95 of a step, every one decided `Take`, fourteen at a
transit on one `Move`.

**The fix** (`World::fold_the_step`, called from `move_bodies` after the step and before the waypoint spend): a body that **landed
on a route point** walks the rest of the step along the next leg - one point at a time, spending each corner as the fold begins,
refused by ground (`clearance_at < 0`) or a body (`radius + other radius`), bounded to two legs, never past the goal, re-stamping
sight after it moves. **Only `Move` and `Hunt` fold**: the tasks whose whole contract is "walk this route".

**Why the narrowing, measured.** The fold applied to every task made the fixture green and the acceptance match **bit-identical**
(fold off 39.5 / 40.3 s, fold on 40.0 / 39.7 s, `entities=138 hash=01a0fb771ee2e75b repaths=761`) - and starved a fixture: a
trebuchet test banked **200 of 400** food and stalled for the remaining **400,000** ticks with **1 repath**. The trace: one
gatherer alternated every tick between **(394394, 313527)** and **(395101, 313901)**, exactly a step apart, from tick 38,000 to
400,000 - the mover walking him 800 toward his route on odd ticks, `settle_workers` walking him 800 back onto his gather place's
standoff on even ones. Two passes, two aims, and the fold's extra 800 kept them permanently out of phase. A gather's approach is
*already* steered by the settle pass, so it is out of this rule's scope; an attacker's stop distance is a range, not a route point,
which is why `Attack` is out too.

**The attempt before it**, kept because the next reader will try it: spending corners *before* the step makes the aim the point
beyond them, which **cuts** the corner - a walker wedged against a forest edge for **68 ticks**, `Slide` at **1 raw unit** a tick.

**Commits us to.** A walk is whole steps on the route's own measure, and no future mover change may reintroduce a clamp to a
corner; the corner is walked through, or the body stands. The goal stays an exact landing, because that is what arrival is built
on. And a fixture the owner asked for is never `#[ignore]`d without his word - when the fix will not land, the answer is to find
out why, not to switch the test off.


### D253 - the slide is the last source of half-steps, and both fixes are refuted (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*Attempted on the owner's `Proceed`, after the adversarial review named the fold's refused-corner gap. **Nothing landed**: the
gap it found is real, the two designs that close it are refuted by measurement, and the question left is the owner's.*

**The rule's remaining violation.** `whole_steps.rs` passes on open ground. With a body parked half a tile past the first corner,
the same walk breaks the rule **567 times in 1,398 walking ticks** - the man creeps at **82, 81, 80... raw units** a tick where a
step is **800**. The cause is `StepDecision::Slide`, the ground slide: it takes the step's **axis component**, so a diagonal aimed
mostly along the blocked axis moves a fraction of a step. The mover never lands on a route point, so no fold can repair it.

**Design A, refuted**: extend the slide to a full step along the clear axis. **16 tests across 10 binaries** regress - a rally
walk, two walks round a building, a felled tree's gap, a shared woodcutting tile, and then fights, training, a trebuchet and a
whole scenario, because a longer slide changes where men stand - all from one cause: a full-length slide walks a man further than
the geometry planned.

**Design B, refuted**: stand instead of a fractional slide and let the repath answer. **14 tests across 8 binaries** regress -
animals and herding, gathering, depletion, a partial load, fights, the line upgrade, the scenario, the crowd - because a man who
cannot slide round a wall wedges, which is what D188 was written from.

**Why it is a fork and not a defect to patch.** Read out of the original on 2026-11-17 (`doIntelligentMovementUpdate`, `008a4360`,
in `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`): a step is a **velocity applied whole**, the new position is then **tested**, and every
collision answer is a **repath** (`We have %d non-past collisions and %d terrain collisions, repathing`), a **pause** enforced by
a priority comparison (`TOLD TO PAUSE BY UNIT %d`), or a stop. **No axis is ever dropped** - the slide does not exist there. And a
reached waypoint is **snapped to and spent in the same update** (`Teleporting to exact waypoint` + `Incrementing waypoint`), which
is what `fold_the_step` now does and what stops a corner costing a tick.

So the slide is ours, added by D188 because a villager that could not slide wedged for 68 ticks - and the game's own answer to that
case is the repath-plus-pause pair our mover does not have in full. *Does a slide count as walking?* The game's answer is that
there is nothing to count: a blocked body either yields the tick or plans again.

**Recorded so it is not re-attempted blind**: the gate that stands a man whose corner remainder is refused was written, uses the
fold's own `fold_leg` so the two cannot disagree, and was **not landed** - the only fixture that drives it also drives the creep,
so it would have been untested code. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-17-the-slide-and-the-rule.md`.


### D254 - following the game on the slide: the rule holds, and the wall is a disagreement (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner, after the reading: **"Follow the game."** Attempted; the engine is **unchanged** and this records what the attempt
found, because the finding is sharper than the change would have been.*

**What was tried.** The terrain slide was deleted outright - the original applies its step whole and answers a collision with a
repath or a pause (`docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`) - with the owner's fixture written first: the same walk with a body parked
half a tile past the first corner, asserting every walking tick is one step or a stand. **Red before**: 82, 81, 80... raw units a
tick, **567 of 1,398** walking ticks short. **Green after**: no slide, no creep, and the walk still costs the ticks its geometry
owes. That part is the rule working exactly as asked.

**Then the suite went red: 14 tests across 8 binaries** (192 of 200 binaries green) - `a_live_animal_is_a_gather_source`,
`the_villager_follows_the_sheep`, `the_shepherd_kills_the_sheep_and_the_gathering_resumes_on_the_body`,
`a_depleted_node_stops_yielding`, `a_farm_starts_with_a_worker_standing_on_it`,
`a_partial_load_comes_home_when_the_node_runs_out`, `a_boar_that_loses_interest_returns_to_where_it_was_struck`,
`a_melee_blow_never_becomes_an_arrow`, `a_refused_retaliation_is_recorded_rather_than_swallowed`,
`a_second_blow_turns_a_boar_that_had_given_up`, `the_skirmish_only_refuses_what_the_fight_has_taken`,
`the_spear_line_upgrades_the_units_the_player_already_has`, `the_ten_minute_scenario_builds_trains_and_fights`, and the crowd
fixture that already fails.

**The diagnosis, and it is not the slide.** Traced: a gatherer ordered onto a sheep stops at **(316980, 316980)** with
`WaitGround` from tick 40 and `stalled` climbing to **267**; his route has three points and does not move. His aim is refused by
`step_is_walkable`'s own clause - the landing `next < 0`, he is clear `now >= 0` - so the last leg of a route the pathfinder
called **reachable** is a step the mover refuses. Raising the ground re-plan budget from **2 to 40** changed nothing: the re-plan
returns the same route, because the route is not wrong and the step test is.

**So the wall is this**: we have **two measures of "walkable"** - the pathfinder grows every blocked tile by the body's radius and
counts the goal reachable, and the mover's step test refuses the landing that overlaps a grown tile - and the game has **one**
(a single collision query at the new position). The slide has been papering over the disagreement by letting a man creep along the
axis the grown tile left free.

**What that costs to fix**, and why it is not this slice: unifying the two measures touches **D176** - the disc rule the owner
asked for after seeing a villager with its disc inside a wall - so it needs its own fixtures on both sides (a node approach must
land, and a body must not end inside a wall), and it is a mover change with the whole crowd surface behind it.

**Attempts recorded so the next reader starts ahead**: a full-length slide regressed **16 tests / 10 binaries**; standing instead
of sliding, with the old budget, regressed **14 tests / 8 binaries**; standing with the budget raised to 40 still regressed the
same animals family. Review: `docs/reviews/2026-11-17-the-slide-and-the-rule.md`.


### D255 - no sliding, and the reason it cannot land yet: a tile is not an object (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner, correcting the rule and the direction in one message: **"man stands or walks. No acceleration or deceleration"** -
not "one whole step" - and **"follow the game. No sliding."** Attempted again with that correction; the engine is unchanged and
this records where it stops, because the stopping point is now a single, named piece of missing model.*

**The rule, in his words.** Constant speed: a man moves at his speed or he does not move, and nothing ramps. "One whole step a
tick" is only the observable form of that at a fixed tick rate, and the two fixtures are written to say so
(`crates/sim/tests/whole_steps.rs`).

**What lands conceptually.** With the terrain slide deleted, the owner's corner fixture - a body parked half a tile past the first
corner - goes from **82, 81, 80...** raw units a tick and **567 of 1,398** walking ticks short to **green**: every walking tick is
one step or a stand. That is his rule, exactly.

**What it breaks, and why the break is the useful part.** The suite then has **14 red tests across 8 binaries** (192 of 200 green),
animals and gathering first: a gatherer ordered onto a sheep stops at **(316980, 316980)** with `WaitGround` from tick 40 and
`stalled` at **267**. The refusal is a disc overlap of **164 raw units - 0.008 of a tile** - against a blocked tile, and no
re-plan budget fixes it (40 instead of 2 changed nothing) because the route the pathfinder returns is the same route.

**And the fix is narrower than it first looked.** The next attempt - step by the **tile grid alone** (the disc test removed, D176's
guarantee left to placement) - took the no-slide suite from **14 red tests across 8 binaries to 3**, of which one is the crowd
fixture that already failed: what is left is `a_villager_walking_beside_a_building_keeps_its_body_clear` (the disc rule itself) and
`a_newcomer_does_not_move_the_working_gatherers` (a gatherer displaced by a newcomer). So the model slice is two rules wide, not a
rewrite: **a building's footprint is exact, a node's trunk is not**, and one fixture about who keeps his place.

**The two fixtures pin opposite sides.** Allow that 0.008-tile brush (the game's collision is against the *object*, and a body
against a trunk or a wall face brushes the tile) and `a_villager_walking_beside_a_building_keeps_its_body_clear` fails: it demands
`body_clearance >= 0` on **every** tick. Refuse it and the sheep fixture fails. There is no single threshold that satisfies both,
because both are honest about different things: **our blocked tile is a whole tile; the game's obstacle is an object with bounds.**

**So the next slice is the model, not the mover**, and the binary and the decompilation say exactly what it is
(`docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`, section of 2026-11-17): **ground is a per-tile test at a point** (`FUN_008aa480` - no radius
anywhere in it), and **things are boxes with a `(radius_x, radius_y)` pair**, with the game's own distance function measuring to
the box so that everything inside a footprint is distance zero
(`compute_distance_sq`, `src/unit/unit_action_build_77a0.cpp`). Overlap is then `distance-to-box < radius`: a man at **half a
diameter** from a tree touches nothing, and a body never enters a building's footprint - which is D176's guarantee, obtained the
game's way rather than by growing tiles.

That also corrects an option this project offered the owner: "strict, no part of the body may overlap a blocked tile" is **not**
his rule and not the game's - it is D176 applied to the wrong question, the pathfinder's grown tile used at stepping time. His
half-diameter rule *is* the game's rule.


### D256 - copy the game: the step now asks the right question, and the route still asks the wrong one (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: **"Copy the game."** Done on the step side in one evening; the reason it cannot land is a second, different site, and
it is named exactly.*

**What was built.** `step_is_walkable` no longer grows every blocked tile by the body's radius (the pathfinder's trick, asked at
stepping time). It asks the game's two questions instead: the **tile under the point** (already there - `free(landing)`), and
**"does my disc overlap a building's footprint box?"** (`disc_touches_a_building`, box distance against `footprint_rect`, which is
`compute_distance_sq`'s measure from the decompilation). The terrain slide is gone with it: a refused step is a repath or a stand.

**What it fixed, measured**: the sheep family's refusal is no longer the coarse tile. Traced, the only refusal left on
`the_villager_follows_the_sheep` is **269 ticks of `refuse building`** - the gatherer squeezing past the **town centre's
footprint**, his disc overlapping it by a hair on a route that hugs the wall.

**And that is the real second site**: `crates/sim/src/path.rs` has **no radius in it at all** - the search runs over free tiles,
so a villager's 0.2-tile body plans a **point** route along the TC's edge and the mover then refuses the step the plan chose. The
original does not do that: its search answers for *"the boundaries of where this unit's radii will go"*
(`doIntelligentMovementUpdate`'s own string), i.e. the walkable area is shrunk by the unit's radius **before** the search.

So "copy the game" is two halves and only one is done: **plan on ground a disc can occupy, and step with the box test.** The
pathfinder slice is the other half, and it is the one with the crowd behind it - which is why it is not started at 02:00 with a
reboot at 04:00.

**Also refuted this evening, for the trail**: with the step test removed entirely (tile-grid only) the no-slide suite is **3 red**
(one of them the crowd fixture that already fails); with the box test added back it is the same 3 plus the animals family's 3,
all of them the TC-edge route above.


### D257 - copy the game, attempted in full: three pieces built, and the wall is the gather place (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: **"Copy the game."** Three pieces were built and measured in one stretch. Each is the game's own model, each is
reverted, and the reason they cannot land together is now precise: **the place a gatherer is sent to is chosen without the body's
box in mind**, and that is a different subsystem from the mover.*

**Piece 1 - the step's two questions.** Ground tested at the tile under the point; a building's footprint tested as a **box**
against the body's radius (depth = `radius - distance to the box`), with D192's rule for a body already touching (it may walk
along, it may not go deeper); the terrain slide deleted. Result: the coarse-tile refusal is gone - the **164-raw (0.008-tile)**
brush that stopped a gatherer 267 ticks is no longer a refusal.

**Piece 2 - the route planned for the body.** The original's search answers for *"the boundaries of where this unit's radii will
go"*, so `pull_route_avoiding` may only cut a corner when the segment stays out of every building footprint grown by the radius
(slab test against axis-aligned boxes, plan time only). Result: the same refusal, unchanged - **because the route was never the
problem**.

**Piece 3 - the place chosen for the body.** The gather standoff may not be a point the mover can never stand on, so candidates
inside a building's inflated box are rejected. Result: the man then had **no place at all** (`Standoff::NoRoom`) and stood where he
was: `the_villager_follows_the_sheep` still fails, now for the honest reason.

**What that says.** The mover now asks the game's questions; what is left is that `standoff_point` picks places by *tile* and
*spacing*, with no notion of the body's box - so a place can be legal by tiles and illegal by geometry, and rejecting those leaves
none. The fix is inside the gather approach (place selection + the ring's geometry), which is D202/D204/D243's ground, not the
mover's, and it is the next slice: **a place is a point where the body fits, and the approach is a route the body can walk.**

**Also measured, for the next reader**: with only Piece 1 (step model, tile grid) the no-slide suite is **3 red** of 200 binaries
(one of them the crowd fixture that already failed) - 197 green. That is the state to resume from: the step model is worth landing
once the place model can live with it.


### D258 - proved from the binary: box against box, and our trees are the wrong size (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: **"Proved and follow the original game and decomp."** Three functions read end to end, and they settle the question
this project has been circling: the game collides **boxes**, not tiles, and every object's box comes from its own radii.*

**The proof** (written out with the code in `docs/archive/research/movement-in-the-binary.md`):

1. **Ground is a point test** - `FUN_008aa480` compares the tile's bits with the unit's passability mask; arguments cast to `int`,
   no radius in it.
2. **Things are AABB boxes** - `FUN_00840830` builds each object's box from its radius table (`obj+0x20 + index*4` over four
   direction indices), grows the query box by the mover's radius, and collides on `<=` in every axis: touching edges collide.
3. **Distance is box-to-box with overlap clamped to zero** - `func_002690E0`/`func_00269190`/`func_00269220` in
   `src/unit/unit_action_distance.cpp` compute `max(0, |dx| - radius_x)` per axis and then the hypotenuse; the movement update
   compares that with `rangeDistance`. **The owner's half-diameter rule is that function at range zero.**

**What it corrects.** Our blocked ground is a tile grid, so the box our step test sees for a **tree is one whole tile** where the
dat describes a trunk a fraction of it. That is why a gatherer was refused a **164-raw (0.008-tile)** brush and stood 267 ticks -
and why the terrain slide looked necessary. The refusal against the **town centre's footprint** is, by the same reading, **right**:
the game calls that a collision too, and the answer is a route that keeps the body's radius clear - which is what its own log
string says the search does.

**Correction, in the same evening** (recorded because it is the kind of claim that sticks): I wrote that our trees were the wrong
size. **They are not** - `TREEA` carries `radius = [0.5, 0.5, 2.0]`, so a tree's box *is* its tile, and our tile grid agrees with
the dat. The **164-raw** refusal was against the **town centre's footprint**, and by the game's own `<=` collision the original
would refuse it too.

**So the next slice is the route and the place, not the box**: the planned polyline must be checked against every building's
footprint grown by the body's radius (`short_range_clear` plans a straight line and nothing validates it), and a gather place must
be a point where the body's box fits. Buildings already have exact boxes, units already have radii, and the ground keeps its point
test. That is the piece that lets "no sliding" land.


### D259 - why every piece so far has failed: the mover walks *at* waypoints, not along the route (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*Attempted again with the route checked against building boxes. Refuted, and the refutation names the actual shape of the defect -
which is worth more than the fourth patch.*

**What was built.** `World::route_clear_of_buildings`: every segment of a planned polyline tested against each building's footprint
grown by the body's radius (slab test, plan time only), and `short_range_clear`'s answer discarded when it fails, so the tile
search answers instead. With the slide still in place the suite is unchanged (green); with the slide **removed** the animals family
fails exactly as before - **3 red**.

**Why it must fail**, and this is the finding: the mover does not follow the polyline. On every tick it walks a **straight line
from wherever it stands to the next waypoint** (`collide` + `step_towards`). Checking the planned segments therefore proves
nothing about the walk: the man leaves the polyline the moment he is nudged, paused, or lands mid-tick (the fold moves him
off it by design), and the next tick's straight line is a *new* segment that nothing has tested. Around a building that segment
cuts the corner by a fraction - **164 raw, 0.008 of a tile** - and the box test refuses it, correctly.

The original does not have this shape: its waypoints are *reached and snapped to* (`Teleporting to exact waypoint`, `Incrementing
waypoint`), its search answers for the unit's radii, and its collision answer is a repath. Ours walks at points and validates
plans.

**So the next slice is a design change, not a patch**: the mover must walk the route it was given - leg by leg, the fold carrying
a landed corner into the next leg (which it already does within a tick), with the *straight-at-the-waypoint* shortcut replaced by
"aim along the current leg". That is what makes a validated plan mean something, and it is where "no sliding" can finally land:
once the walk is confined to the route, a blocked straight line is not a case the mover has to improvise around.

**Everything measured tonight, in one place**: slide removed alone - **14 red / 8 binaries**; step model (point ground + building
box) - **3 red**; plus disc-aware pull, box-clear places, and route validation - **still 3 red**, all animals, all one straight
line clipping one footprint. None landed; the engine is unchanged.


### D260 - the original turns before it walks, and our mover has no facing (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner asked how the original and the decomp answer the "straight at the waypoint" defect D259 found. They answer it with a
**facing**: a body moves along its heading, and the heading turns by at most one notch per update.*

**The proof.** `src/zone/zone_spatial_entity_adjust_heading_step.cpp` (`func_001DF350`) turns the facing by
`2*pi/count` with `count` floored at **8** - i.e. **45 degrees a notch** - and the movement update turns **before** it steps
(`Doing yaw of %.10f, limitedYawAngle=%d`, then the movement call), declining a turn it would overshoot (*"NOT Doing yaw ...
because we'll hit the point the next time"*). Arrival is a **snap and spend** (`Teleporting to exact waypoint`,
`Incrementing waypoint`), collisions are **boxes** answered by a repath or a pause, and the search plans for the unit's radii.

**Why that ends the corner problem**: a step is always along the current facing, so there is no straight line to the next waypoint
to clip anything with. A corner is a **turn**, and a turn costs updates.

**What our mover lacks**: a facing. It has no heading state at all - every tick it walks a straight line from wherever it stands to
the next waypoint, which is why five attempts at the plan, the place, the box and the route could not fix a walk that ignores all
of them.

**Correction, same evening, from the owner** - *"Does turn really take time? I remember turns being instant."* **He is right.**
`FUN_008a3270` is `calculateYawAngle()`, and what `maxYawPerSec` limits is the **facing**: `Limited yawAngle to maxYaw of %s`,
`Reversing yawAngle`, over an `interval`. Nothing in the movement update scales the *step* by the yaw - its result feeds a flag,
not a distance - and the 8-way `count` in `adjust_heading_step` is the number of sprite facings, with `a1` notches applied in one
call. **A unit moves in a new direction at once and its picture turns over time.** So "a turn costs ticks" was wrong and is
withdrawn.

**Which puts the corner back on the two pieces that are left, and both are proven**: the original's protection is that the **search
keeps the body's radius clear** (*"the boundaries of where this unit's radii will go"*) and the **waypoint is snapped to**
(`Teleporting to exact waypoint`, `Incrementing waypoint`) - so a short straight step toward the next point is a step along ground
the body fits on. Ours plans for a point and lets the body drift off it, which is how a **164-raw** clip of a footprint appeared.
The slice stays: **plan for the radius, keep the body on the route.**


### D261 - plan for the radius, keep the body on the route: five pieces, and the corner that survives them (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: **"Proceed."** Five pieces built and measured together; none landed; the wall is now a single geometric fact, and the
next step is named.*

**What was built, all at once** (each is the game's own model, from D258/D260's readings):

1. **Radius-aware line test** - `line_clear_body` in `path.rs`: a line must keep the radius clear of every blocked or avoided tile
   within one tile of the path, by slab test against each tile's grown box.
2. **Radius-aware pull** - `pull_route_avoiding` takes the radius and asks the new line test, so a shortcut cannot graze a corner.
3. **Box step test** - `step_is_walkable` asks the tile under the point and a **building's footprint box** (`building_overlap`,
   depth `radius - distance to box`), with D192's rule for a body already touching.
4. **Places and waypoints pushed out of the inflated footprints** (`push_out_of_buildings`).
5. **The slide deleted**, and a plan that fails the box test discarded in favour of the search (`route_clear_of_buildings`).

**What it does, measured**: every fixture green with the slide in place, and **the same 3 red** in the animals family with the
slide out - refused at **`now=0 next=164`**: a landing **164 raw (0.008 tiles)** inside a building's box while clear.

**Why the pieces cannot close it, and this is the finding**: on a **tile-centre** route, a diagonal step past a building's corner
passes *exactly through* that corner, so the body's box overlaps by its **whole radius** (0.2 tiles = 4000 raw) - a test that no
route built from tile centres can pass, and the game does not build one either (see the next entry's numbers: **a town centre's
`radius` is `[2.0, 2.0, 0.0]`, so its box *is* its 4x4 footprint**, and the original would refuse the same step). What the original
has and we do not is a **finer-than-tile** route: its low-level search bends the path *inside* a tile, and our own `short_range_clear`
already borrows that idea for **bodies** ("shoulder points round every body so the detour can bend inside a tile", D211).

**So the next piece is the one shape already in the tree, applied to obstacles**: **shoulder points round a building's corners** -
the route bends a radius clear *inside* the tiles, so its legs never pass through a corner. That is a contained change in
`short_range_clear` (it already builds shoulder points for discs, and a footprint corner is a disc of zero radius at the corner),
and it is the piece that makes 1-5 land.


### D262 - the endpoint is the last uncut corner: 3 red to 1, and the one left is a range (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*Attempted on **"Proceed"** with the shoulder-point plan from D261. The result is the smallest real gain of the evening and it is
worth recording: **one** projected point took the animals family from **3 failures to 1**.*

**What was built**: only the projection of the route's **endpoint** out of every building footprint grown by the body's radius
(`push_out_of_buildings`, the same helper the place search uses), applied in `plan_path` to `finish` - the last leg is the one
unchecked corner in every plan, because the *goal* may sit inside the inflated footprint and then **every** route's final step
clips the wall by a fraction.

**Measured**: `the_villager_follows_the_sheep` and `the_shepherd_kills_the_sheep_and_the_gathering_resumes_on_the_body` go **green**;
`a_live_animal_is_a_gather_source` stays red, and its message has changed - not "did not reach the sheep" any more, but **"must end
up carrying meat"**. He gets there and does not work.

**Why, and it is the next one-line question**: the projection moves him the shortest distance out of the wall, which is *away from
the node*, and the gather's arrival test is a **standoff distance**, not the game's **box gap** (`func_002690E0`: `max(0, |dx| -
radius_x)`, compared with `rangeDistance`). Pushed 0.2 tiles out, he is outside the standoff and never starts.

**So the option, and it is the game's own rule**: make "at the node" the game's measure - the **box gap** between worker and node
within the order's **range** - instead of a ring distance. Then a man pushed out of a wall by his own width is still working,
because the gap he is measured by is the gap the original measures. That is one function (`reaches`/`at_node`) and it is the last
piece of the same model.


### D263 - two pieces land in the ledger, and the wall is now a place with coordinates (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*Attempted the box-gap arrival rule and the endpoint projection together. Neither is in the tree; both are measured, and the
failure now has an address.*

**Piece that works, measured**: projecting the **route's endpoint** out of every building footprint grown by the body's radius
(`push_out_of_buildings`, from `plan_path`'s `finish`) takes the animals family from **3 failures to 1**. The last leg is the one
unchecked corner in every plan, because the *goal* can sit inside the inflated footprint.

**Piece that does not**: rejecting gather places that fall outside the pair's reach after that projection. It changes nothing on
the failing case, and the trace explains why.

**The failure, with coordinates**: `a_live_animal_is_a_gather_source` sends a villager to a sheep **6 tiles** from the town centre
(tile 18,18). He walks and stops at **(362642, 316792)** - the **south wall of the town centre** (rows 12-15), **2.16 tiles** short
of the sheep, `at_node=false` for the rest of the run. He is not 8.66 tiles short any more (the endpoint projection moved him 6.5
tiles), but he cannot bend round the corner: his route's legs clip the footprint by a fraction and the step test refuses them, and
the re-plan budget runs out returning the same route.

**So the next piece is the one D261 named, and the tree already contains the planner for it**: `short_range_clear` grows every
blocked tile by the body's radius (the Minkowski sum), builds a **visibility graph over the grown rectangles' corners**, and adds
**shoulder points** round every body so a detour can bend *inside* a tile. That is the game's "low-level path". The failing
approach is 6 tiles long - exactly its job - so the question to answer next is **why the tile search answered instead**, and the
recommendation is to route short approaches through `short_range_clear` first and only fall back to the tile search when it
returns `None`.


### D264 - the planner was never asked a question it could answer (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*The owner: **"Proceed."** One small change, one real defect, and the slide's exact role in the ledger.*

**The defect**: `short_range_clear` does the game's job - it grows every obstruction by the body's radius (a Minkowski sum), builds
a visibility graph over the grown rectangles' corners and adds shoulder points round bodies (D211) - and it was **always passed a
goal it could not reach**. A gather approach aims at the **node**: a tree's tile, a sheep's tile, a mill's wall. All blocked
ground. Grown by the radius, the goal is *inside* an obstruction, the graph has no node for it, and the function returns `None` -
so the **tile search** answered every gather approach in the game, and the good planner was dead code on that path.

**The change**: `World::legal_standoff(at, radius)` - the nearest point near the aim where the body fits (clearance at least zero
and outside every footprint grown by its radius), found by stepping out along eight directions in eighths of a tile. The
short-range planner is given **that** point as its goal; the arrival test then decides whether the worker can work from there.

**Measured**: animals **11 of 11 green** (they were 3 red at D263), `whole_steps` 2 green, `body_clearance` 2 green.

**And the slide, measured rather than argued**: then deleted, with the planner now given a legal goal, **the animals family goes
back to 3 red** - `a_live_animal_is_a_gather_source`, `the_villager_follows_the_sheep`,
`the_shepherd_kills_the_sheep_and_the_gathering_resumes_on_the_body`. The route is not the problem any more; the **place** is. A
gatherer keeps to his place to within a fifth of a tile (`settle_workers`), those nudges are far under a step, and a rule that
refuses anything but a whole step leaves him a fraction short and he never works. The original does not have this category: its
movement is **continuous**, 0.04 tiles a tick (D258), so "a fraction of a step" is a normal step to it.

**So the slide stays, and D253's creep is its cost, not its purpose.** The sequence is now clear and it is the last piece of this
whole thread: **`settle_workers` must stop asking for movements smaller than a step** - the game walks a worker to his place and
then stands him, it never nudges him a fraction of a step - and then the slide can go. That is a place/waypoint question in
`settle_workers`, not a movement question.

**A correction of wording, prompted by the owner ("Where did you get 'only whole steps' from?")**: *"one whole step"* is **my
phrase, not his**. He said **"man stands or walks. No acceleration or deceleration."** The step is only how constant speed looks at
a fixed tick rate, and the fixture measures it because that is observable. What actually blocks the slide is not the *size* of a
step: it is that `settle_workers` asks for a **sub-step nudge** (a fifth of a tile at most), which a constant-speed mover has no way
to express - and which the original never asks for, because it walks a worker onto his place and leaves him standing. The fold
(D252) already carries the remainder past a waypoint inside the same tick (the game's *"Teleporting to exact waypoint"*,
*"Incrementing waypoint"*), so a short tick is not the issue either.


### D265 - the refusal, traced; and a correction to D264's explanation (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided

*"Proceed" on the next step. Nothing landed; the trace is worth more than the patch, and one of D264's claims was wrong.*

**The trace**: slide deleted, `the_villager_follows_the_sheep` instrumented at the refusal point. The villager refuses **270 times**
from tick 31, always from the same place:

    REFUSE id=2 tick=31 here=(316980,316980) step=(566,566)  clear=-530
    REFUSE id=2 tick=32 here=(316980,316980) step=(793,-104) clear=-164     (repeats to tick 300+)

`clearance_at` is the *landing's* clearance for his 0.2 disc, so **-164 raw = 0.008 tiles** inside a grown obstruction, and
**-530 = 0.0265**. He is standing legally (`now >= 0`) and every step would take him inside by a hair - which is D192's rule firing
correctly (`next < 0 && now >= 0`).

**The correction**: D264 said the animals family fails without the slide because `settle_workers` keeps a place "to within a fifth
of a tile" with nudges under a step. **Reading the code refutes it**: the settle writes `entity.position` **directly** - it does not
go through `move_bodies`, so the step rule never sees those moves and cannot refuse them. The three reds are the **mover refusing
its own route**, not the settle. D264's sentence is left in place above as the record of what I claimed; this entry is what the
code says.

**Tried and refuted in the same sitting** (seventh variant, same residual): a fine-sampled (`scale/8`) body-aware leg test
(`leg_is_walkable`) plus a standoff that prefers a point whose leg from the nearest body is walkable. **Still 3 red of 11.** So the
grazing leg is **not** the final leg to the aim: it is a leg *inside* the planned polyline, or each tick's aim is re-derived so the
"nearest body" test is answering about a different moment.

**What the next measurement is, and it is a measurement**: take the route `short_range_clear` returns for this fixture and walk its
legs in order with `leg_is_walkable`; the **first** failing leg names the stage that produced it - the grown-corner graph, the pull
(whose own line test is *tile*-based, `line_clear_avoiding`, so a pulled shortcut can graze for a body), or the raw final leg.
Seven variants have failed by reasoning about which stage it is; one trace of the actual polyline settles it.


### D266 - the owner's two rules are fixtures, and the fixtures are scenes: measured, both rules are broken elsewhere (2026-11-17)

*Date:* 2026-11-17

*Area:* Pathfinding & movement
*Status:* decided
